svg.title: The producer's image replacement, and the two things that must cross the exec
svg.text: A producer reload crosses one exec, and two process resources have to survive it
Left lane: the image being replaced. Right lane: the replacement. Only one process exists throughout; the pid never changes.
image A — the producer that was armed
SIGALRM poll: every 1 s, compute the code stamp
stamp != the one recorded at arming
throwaway import proof of the new image
proof fails: keep this image, print one line
take the seat, rewrite its record with the new stamp
the replacement is a new image in the same process
Carried across: the seat's open advisory lock, as an inheritable descriptor — the lock is released by any close, so re-entering it in the replacement races the release.
Not carried: the interval timer. It belongs to the process, not the image, so it fires in image B before B installs its own handler — where the default disposition kills it. Disarmed at the exec.
